hindi: आयु, कर्म, धन, विद्या और मृत्यु — ये पाँच देहधारी के गर्भ में रहते हुए ही निश्चय रच दिए जाते हैं।
english: Lifespan, action, wealth, learning and death: these five are indeed created for the embodied being right while he is in the womb.
notes: Five items listed with ca after several of them; the verb sṛjyante is passive (are created), with no agent stated.

hindi: पुत्र, मित्र और बन्धु उन साधुओं से लौट जाते हैं; और जो उनके साथ जाने वाले हैं, उस धर्म से कुल सुकृत (सुकर्मों वाला) होता है।
english: From the good, they turn back: sons, friends, kinsmen. And those who will go with them: from that dharma the family is well done.
notes: Obscure verse; the construction of the second line is uncertain. 'te' is taken as referring to putra-mitrāṇi bāndhavāḥ, and 'taiḥ' as the good (sādhubhyaḥ). 'tad-dharmāt' is taken as 'from that dharma' (ablative of source/reason); 'sukṛtam kulam' is taken as 'the family is well done (a family of good deeds)' with no verb stated. The relative clause 'ye ... gantāraḥ' has no stated main clause. Sense of the whole is not certain.

hindi: दर्शन, ध्यान और स्पर्श से मछली, कछुई और पक्षिणी अपने बच्चे का सदा पालन करती है; वैसे ही सज्जनों की संगति।
english: By sight, thought and touch, the female fish, the female tortoise and the female bird constantly protect the young one; likewise the company of good people.
notes: Verb pālayate is singular though three subjects are listed (each taken separately). The verb of the 'company of good people' clause is not stated; the sentence is left as in the Sanskrit. 'śiśum' is singular (the young one); the possessive 'their own' is not in the text.

hindi: जब तक यह शरीर स्वस्थ है और जब तक मृत्यु दूर है, तब तक अपना हित कर लेना चाहिए; प्राण के अन्त में क्या करेगा?
english: As long as this body is healthy indeed, and as long as death is far away, so long one should do what is good for oneself; at the end of life, what will one do?
notes: Subject of kariṣyati is the unstated 'one'.

words.gloss: having the qualities of the wish-granting cow (kāmadhenu)

hindi: विद्या कामधेनु के गुणों वाली है; वह निश्चय ही अकाल (असमय) में फल देने वाली है। प्रवास में विद्या माता के समान है; विद्या को गुप्त धन कहा गया है।
english: Learning has the qualities of the wish-granting cow (kāmadhenu); it indeed gives fruit out of season. In a foreign land, learning is like a mother; learning is held to be hidden wealth.
notes: 'smṛtam' (lit. remembered) is rendered 'is held', i.e. is declared in tradition. 'akāle' could also be 'at the wrong time'. 'phala' (fruit) is not specified further.

hindi: एक भी गुणवान पुत्र हो; गुणहीन सौ से क्या? एक चन्द्रमा अन्धकार को नष्ट करता है, और हजारों तारे नहीं।
english: Even one son possessed of virtue: what use are a hundred without virtue? The one moon destroys darkness, and not the stars by the thousand.
notes: The first half has no verb; 'kim' with the instrumental is taken as 'what use is ...'. The thought 'one virtuous son is enough' is left implicit as in the Sanskrit.

words.gloss: for as long as life lasts

hindi: मूर्ख चिरायु होकर जन्मा हो तो भी; इसलिए जन्म लेते ही मरा हुआ श्रेष्ठ है। और वह मरा हुआ थोड़े दुःख के लिए होता है; जड़ जीवन भर जलाएगा।
english: A fool, even if born long-lived: therefore one dead at birth is better. And dead, he is for little sorrow; the dullard would burn for as long as life lasts.
notes: 'dahet' has no object stated (those who suffer are unstated). 'jaḍaḥ' = dull, stupid (the fool). 'yāvaj-jīvam' = for the whole of life.

words.gloss: service of one devoid of family

hindi: बुरे गाँव में वास, कुलहीन की सेवा, बुरा भोजन, क्रोधी मुख वाली पत्नी, और मूर्ख पुत्र, और विधवा कन्या — ये छह बिना अग्नि के शरीर को जला देते हैं।
english: Living in a bad village, service of one devoid of family, bad food, and a wife with an angry face, and a son who is a fool, and a daughter who is a widow: six burn up the body without fire.
notes: The six items are listed in lines a to c and summed up by ṣaṭ in line d. 'kulahīna' = devoid of family (low-born in sense; not stated further). 'kanyā' = daughter/girl.

hindi: उस गाय से क्या किया जाता है जो न दूध देने वाली है, न गर्भिणी? उस उत्पन्न पुत्र से क्या प्रयोजन जो न विद्वान है, न भक्तिमान?
english: What is done with that cow which is neither a milch cow nor with calf? What purpose is there in a son born who is neither learned nor devoted?
notes: 'garbhiṇī' (lit. pregnant) is applied to a cow, hence 'with calf'. The object of devotion (bhakti) is not stated.

words.gloss: of those scorched by the heat of saṃsāra (worldly round)

hindi: संसार के ताप से झुलसे हुओं के लिए तीन विश्राम के कारण हैं: सन्तान और पत्नी, और सज्जनों की संगति ही।
english: For those scorched by the heat of saṃsāra (the worldly round), three are causes of rest: offspring and wife, and the company of the good indeed.
notes: The verb 'are' is not stated. 'satām saṅgatiḥ' = company of the good; 'eva' is rendered 'indeed'.

hindi: राजा एक बार बोलते हैं, पण्डित एक बार बोलते हैं, कन्याएँ एक बार दी जाती हैं; ये तीन, एक बार, एक बार।
english: Kings speak once, learned men speak once, girls are given once: these three, once, once.
notes: The repetition 'sakṛt sakṛt' is kept as printed (once, once). 'jalpanti' = speak (a statement). 'pradīyante' is passive; the giver is unstated.

hindi: अकेले से तप, दो से पठन, तीन से गायन; चार से गमन, पाँच से खेत, बहुतों से रण।
english: Austerity with one alone, study with two, singing with three; travel with four, a field with five, war with many.
notes: No verb is stated; the verse is a list of activity paired with number of persons. 'kṣetram' = field (as printed; farming is not stated). Printed 'bahubhī' is regular sandhi for bahubhiḥ before raṇaḥ.

hindi: वही पत्नी है जो पवित्र और दक्ष है, वही पत्नी है जो पतिव्रता है; वही पत्नी है जो पति से प्रेम रखने वाली है, वही पत्नी है जो सत्य बोलने वाली है।
english: She is a wife who is pure and skilled; she is a wife who is devoted to her husband; she is a wife who is fond of her husband; she is a wife who speaks the truth.
notes: 'pati-prītā' is ambiguous (pleased with her husband, or dear to him); 'fond of her husband' is chosen. 'pati-vratā' = whose vow is her husband.

hindi: पुत्रहीन का घर शून्य है; बन्धुहीनों के लिए दिशाएँ शून्य हैं; मूर्ख का हृदय शून्य है; दरिद्रता सब ओर से शून्य है।
english: The house of the sonless is empty; for the kinless the directions are empty; the heart of a fool is empty; poverty is empty in everything.
notes: Line a is irregular: 'abāndhavāḥ' is masculine plural and cannot agree with feminine 'diśaḥ'; the sense taken is 'for the kinless the directions are empty', and 'tu' (but) is not separately rendered because the clause has no contrast to carry it. This is an interpretation, not settled. 'sarva-śūnyā' could be 'empty of all' or 'wholly empty'.

hindi: अभ्यास के बिना शास्त्र विष है, अजीर्ण में भोजन विष है; दरिद्र के लिए गोष्ठी विष है, वृद्ध के लिए तरुणी विष है।
english: Without practice, a treatise is poison; in indigestion, food is poison; for a poor man, an assembly is poison; for an old man, a young woman is poison.
notes: 'goṣṭhī' = assembly, gathering of people. Genitives 'daridrasya', 'vṛddhasya' are taken as 'for'.

hindi: दया से रहित धर्म को छोड़ देना चाहिए, विद्या से हीन गुरु को छोड़ देना चाहिए; क्रोधी मुख वाली पत्नी को छोड़ देना चाहिए, स्नेहरहित बन्धुओं को छोड़ देना चाहिए।
english: One should abandon a dharma devoid of compassion; one should abandon a teacher devoid of learning; one should abandon a wife with an angry face; one should abandon kinsmen devoid of affection.

hindi: यात्रा देहधारियों के लिए बुढ़ापा है, जल पर्वतों के लिए बुढ़ापा है; मैथुन का अभाव स्त्रियों के लिए बुढ़ापा है, धूप वस्त्रों के लिए बुढ़ापा है। और इन्द्रियों को संयम में रखकर बगुले के समान पण्डित मनुष्य देश, काल और बल को जानकर सब कार्य सिद्ध करे।
english: A journey is old age for embodied beings, water is old age for mountains; non-intercourse is old age for women, sun-heat is old age for clothes. And having restrained the senses like a heron, a learned man, having known place, time and strength, would accomplish all tasks.
notes: GROUPING: this unit joins two verses; lines a-b (the 'jarā' verse) and lines c-d (the 'indriyāṇi ca saṃyamya bakavat' verse) are separate verses of two lines each and should be two units. 'adhvā' is taken as 'journey' (adhvan, road). 'deśa-kāla-balam' singular accusative, taken as a dvandva in collective sense.

hindi: कौन-सा काल है, कौन-से मित्र हैं, कौन-सा देश है, आय और व्यय कौन-से हैं, मैं कौन हूँ और मेरी शक्ति क्या है — इस प्रकार बार-बार सोचना चाहिए।
english: What is the time, which are the friends, what is the place, what are the expense and income, and who am I and what is my power: thus it is to be pondered again and again.
notes: The repeated 'what/who' is a series of questions with no verb stated. 'vyaya-āgamau' = expense and income (dual).

hindi: द्विजातियों के लिए अग्नि देवता है, मुनियों के लिए देवता हृदय में है; अल्पबुद्धि वालों के लिए प्रतिमा है, समदर्शी के लिए सर्वत्र।
english: For the twice-born, fire is the god; for sages, the deity is in the heart; for those of little intelligence, the image; for one who sees equally, everywhere.
notes: Elliptical verse: the genitives are taken as 'for'. In the last pāda 'samadarśinaḥ' is read as genitive singular (parallel to the preceding genitives); it could also be nominative plural. 'sarvatra' is left without a stated noun (the deity is understood).
